claims.text: The starting Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles are initially solid, well-mixed, and single-phase.
Stochastic local atomic arrangements govern the premelting and melting behavior of Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles.
Stochastic atomic arrangements produce heterogeneous short-range order.
The heterogeneous local arrangements produce a spatial distribution of binding energies.
Local elemental-composition variations arise from stochastic atomic arrangements.
Local elemental-composition variations are accompanied by strain fields.
Slight elemental segregation and element-dependent binding strengths create regions with locally lower cohesive energy.
Regions with lower local cohesive energy initiate surface premelting.
Surface-premelted regions expand and merge into the particle interior as temperature increases.
The merging of locally premelted regions produces a gradual, broadened transition to complete melting.
Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles will begin surface disordering at a lower temperature than size-matched single-metal or simpler binary nanoparticles.
Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu HEA nanoparticles will exhibit a broader and more gradual melting interval than the baseline particles.
Solid and semi-liquid regions will coexist over a wider temperature range in the HEA nanoparticles than in the baseline particles.
Single-metal or simpler binary nanoparticles have a more uniform binding-energy distribution and a relatively sharp melting point.
The proposed behavior applies primarily at nanoscale sizes where surface effects are significant and may not extend to bulk HEAs.
Particle-to-particle variability may reduce experimental reproducibility.
Absence of either significantly earlier surface premelting or a notably broadened melting transition relative to size-matched simpler particles would falsify the hypothesis.
